children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:
** South Korean shares rose sharply on Friday, as chipmakers tracked overnight gains in US peers, while investors kept an eye on the Bank of Japan's policy decision due later in the day.
** The benchmark KOSPI
was up 121.10 points, or 1.80%, at 6,836.51 as of 0130 GMT.
** For the week, it has fallen 0.9%, after rising 3.3% last week.

** Wall Street bounced back on Thursday as easing oil prices, dropping US Treasury yields and solid labor data helped markets move beyond the Federal Reserve's first interest rate hike in more than three years.

** The Bank of Japan is set to raise interest rates to a 31-year high on Friday and pledge more to counter inflation risks, which may heighten if the start of a U.S. rate-hike cycle weakens the yen against the dollar.
** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics
rose 2.28% and peer SK Hynix
gained 4.30%, after the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index
rose 3.1% on Thursday.
** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
slid 0.55%, while Hyundai Motor
and sister automaker Kia Corp
were up 1.17% and unchanged, respectively.
** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings
shed 0.31%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics
fell 0.29%.
** Of the total 909 traded issues, 457 shares advanced, while 406 declined.
** Foreigners were net buyers of shares worth 157.7 billion won ($113.99 million).
** The won was quoted at 1,384.1 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 0.19% lower than its previous close at 1,381.5.
** In money and debt markets, December futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) gained 0.09 point to 102.30.
** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) fell by 3.5 basis points to 4.023%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
fell by 7.3 basis points to 4.439%.
